rationale: A wins because it gives the founder four genuinely different reporter-shaped stories and attaches the exact proof that makes each one live or die. Its pricing angle, "Nobody has settled on what an AI agent should cost, including Airtable," finds a real business-model story B leaves on the floor. B is competent, but "pre-AI decacorns rebrand to survive" imports a melodrama the fact pattern does not earn.
gaps_in_A: "Airtable drops the spreadsheet label and bets the company on agents" overstates the facts; the update says repositioning and agent launch, not an existential company bet.
"established category leader" and the comparison set "Notion, Smartsheet and Monday" are plausible beat context, but they are not in the supplied update.
"pricing is genuinely open right now, which makes the company an unusually candid example" treats unfinished pricing as candor; the facts only say pricing is not finalized.
gaps_in_B: "pre-AI decacorns rebrand to survive" invents motive and a market narrative; the update gives valuation pressure, not survival stakes.
"the business press is already telling" is an unsupported live-news claim. No prior coverage or current news signal was supplied.
"Airtable's new agents read company records and act on them" is mostly the announcement restated; it needs a sharper editorial lens to avoid launch-note sludge.
It misses the standalone pricing story despite the explicit fact that "pricing for the agent features is not finalized."
